profile.headline: Backend Software Engineer | Java · Spring Boot · Kafka · Kubernetes · TypeScript · AWS | Building AT&T’s reverse logistics platform
profile.summary:
If you've ever traded in or returned a phone on AT&T's network, a system I work on decided where it went and what it was worth. Mostly Java and Spring Boot, about a million of those decisions a month.

That's the third job in a row where the software moves physical things. Pharmacy stock, then freight and trucks, now devices. I didn't plan it, but it turns out I like problems where being wrong costs something you can pick up and hold.

Nights: cali-draw.com, a collaborative whiteboard I built and deployed solo, mostly to learn how WebSockets behave behind a reverse proxy. (Badly. Silently.) And job-pilot, which automates job applications and won't touch LinkedIn, because I'd like to keep this account.  Java · Spring Boot · Kafka · PostgreSQL · TypeScript · React · Kubernetes · AWS

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Backend work on Midas, the routing engine behind AT&T device returns — 1M+ transactions a month deciding disposition, SKU devaluation, and where each device goes next.

- Put a TypeScript pre-classifier in front of the Java rule engine narrowing 900 rules to 20–65 per transaction type before evaluation.

- Migrated 1M+ monthly events from Kafka to Azure Event Hubs with zero data loss over a three-week live cutover.

- Built Nova, a RAG pipeline over the rule definitions so care teams can ask why a device was routed a given way instead of paging engineering.

Java · Spring Boot · Kafka · PostgreSQL · TypeScript · React · Kubernetes · Docker · Jenkins

positions.title: Software Developer - Backend
positions.description:
- Pharmacy inventory and billing platform used across 30 pharmacy accounts — stock levels, reorder triggers, and payment reconciliation.

- Cut stockout incidents by 34% with a reorder service that sets safety-stock thresholds per SKU from an XGBoost demand model trained on 18 months of dispensing history.

- Eliminated duplicate orders under concurrent writes by rebuilding the reorder trigger in Java/Spring Boot as an idempotent workflow on a Kafka inventory-change stream, replacing polling.

- Brought payment reconciliation discrepancies from 2.1% to under 0.1% with idempotent Stripe webhook handling that verifies processor confirmation against internal order state.

Java · Spring Boot · Python · React · TypeScript · Kafka · PostgreSQL · Docker

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
- Warehouse and freight platform for a pulp and paper manufacturer — deciding which truck a shipment goes on and which plant it ships from.

- Cut freight quote turnaround from 45 minutes to under 10 seconds with a rate-shopping engine across 6 carriers, saving $340K a year in expedited freight.

- Reduced failed carrier integrations by 90%, replacing 12 point-to-point EDI connections with one ingestion layer with retry policies and dead-letter routing.

- Eliminated double-booked capacity by redesigning dispatch as an idempotent workflow on a Kafka reservation stream.

projects.title: Cali-Draw — Real-Time Collaborative Whiteboard
projects.description:
A collaborative canvas where several people draw at once and everyone
sees the same thing. Live at cali-draw.com. Built and deployed solo.

Split into three services in a monorepo — Next.js frontend, an
Express API, and a dedicated WebSocket server — because HTTP traffic
is bursty and stateless while socket connections are long-lived and
stateful, and running them together means a spike in one starves the
other.

The interesting problems were the ones that only appear with real
users on it. Browsers won't send an Authorization header on a
WebSocket upgrade, so the token travels as a query parameter and gets
validated before the connection is accepted. A reconnect could
occasionally fire before cookie auth had finished, opening a window
where a socket existed before it was authenticated. And Nginx drops
the handshake entirely if you forget the Upgrade and Connection
headers — no error, no log line, nothing.

PostgreSQL via Prisma, Bun runtime, deployed on EC2 with Docker
Compose behind Nginx, TLS via Certbot.

projects.title: job-pilot — Agentic CLI Pipeline with LLM Guardrails
projects.description:
A CLI that runs a five-step pipeline: scrape a job description,
tailor a LaTeX resume against it, fill the application form, find a
hiring contact, draft the outreach.

The hard part isn't the automation, it's stopping the model from
lying. Letting an LLM rewrite resume content invites exactly one
failure mode — it invents a metric, a company, or a skill that was
never there. The system prompt constrains Claude to editing existing
bullet content only, never adding a claim that isn't already in the
base file.

The other half is knowing where to stop. LinkedIn messaging and
Workday applications are left manual on purpose rather than fought
with brittle evasion, and the first ten runs open a visible browser
and pause before submitting anything. Per-run API cost is measured
and documented, because an agent that takes real-world actions should
be observable before it's autonomous.

TypeScript, Claude API, Playwright, Cheerio, pdflatex, Nodemailer.
